theory.intro: Once two sides of a right-angled triangle are known, every angle in it is fixed. The inverse functions $\sin^{-1}$, $\cos^{-1}$ and $\tan^{-1}$ turn a known ratio back into the angle that produced it.
facts: The ratios are $\sin\theta=\frac{O}{H}$, $\cos\theta=\frac{A}{H}$ and $\tan\theta=\frac{O}{A}$, where $O$, $A$ and $H$ are named **relative to the marked angle**.
Choose the ratio that uses **the two sides you are given**; the third side is never needed.
If $\sin\theta=k$ then $\theta=\sin^{-1}(k)$, and likewise for $\cos^{-1}$ and $\tan^{-1}$.
On a calculator the inverse functions are the **SHIFT** (or **2nd**) functions above the trigonometric keys.
$\sin^{-1}$ is **not** $\frac{1}{\sin}$ — it is the operation that undoes $\sin$.
Both unknown angles of a right-angled triangle are acute, so the inverse function always returns the angle you want.
$1^{\circ}=60'$, so convert a decimal answer such as $41.4096^{\circ}$ with the DMS button, rounding up when the next unit is $30$ or more.
steps: Label the sides relative to the marked angle

foundation.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\coordinate (R) at (3.6,0);\coordinate (T) at (0,2.7);\draw (O)--(R);\draw (O)--(T) node[midway,left] {$6\text{ cm}$};\draw (R)--(T) node[midway,above right] {$10\text{ cm}$};\coordinate (va) at ($(O)!0.3cm!(R)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(O)!0.3cm!(T)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(O)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$\theta$",angle radius=0.62cm,angle eccentricity=1.5] {angle=T--R--O};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Find $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree.
foundation.solution_text:
The $6$ cm side is opposite $\theta$ and the $10$ cm side is the hypotenuse.
$\sin\theta=\frac{6}{10}$
$\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{6}{10}\right)$
$=36.8698\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx37^{\circ}$

mastery.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\coordinate (R) at (1.78606,0);\coordinate (T) at (0,0.9);\draw (O)--(R);\draw (O)--(T) node[midway,left] {$1.8\text{ m}$};\draw[very thick] (R)--(T) node[midway,above right] {$4.0\text{ m}$};\coordinate (va) at ($(O)!0.25cm!(R)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(O)!0.25cm!(T)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(O)$)--(vb);\node at (0.9,-0.55) {Slide A};\coordinate (P) at (2.9,0);\coordinate (Q) at (5.15,0);\coordinate (S) at (2.9,1.05);\draw (P)--(Q) node[midway,below] {$4.5\text{ m}$};\draw (P)--(S) node[midway,left] {$2.1\text{ m}$};\draw[very thick] (Q)--(S);\coordinate (pa) at ($(P)!0.25cm!(Q)$);\coordinate (pb) at ($(P)!0.25cm!(S)$);\draw (pa)--($(pa)+(pb)-(P)$)--(pb);\node at (4.02,-0.55) {Slide B};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Slide A drops $1.8$ m over a sloping surface $4.0$ m long.
Slide B drops $2.1$ m over a horizontal run of $4.5$ m. Which slide is steeper, and by how many degrees, correct to the nearest degree?
mastery.solution_text:
$\sin A=\frac{1.8}{4.0}$
$A=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1.8}{4.0}\right)$
$=26.7436\ldots^{\circ}$
$\tan B=\frac{2.1}{4.5}$
$B=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2.1}{4.5}\right)$
$=25.0168\ldots^{\circ}$
$A-B=1.7267\ldots^{\circ}$
Slide A is the steeper slide, by $2^{\circ}$.

mastery.question_text:
A staircase climbs $2.7$ m in total.
It has $12$ steps and each step has a horizontal tread of $260$ mm.
Find the angle the staircase makes with the floor, correct to the nearest minute.
mastery.solution_text:
$12\times260\text{ mm}=3120\text{ mm}$
$=3.12\text{ m of horizontal run}$
$\tan\theta=\frac{2.7}{3.12}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2.7}{3.12}\right)$
$=40.8724\ldots^{\circ}$
$=40^{\circ}52'20.67''$
$\approx40^{\circ}52'$

mastery.question_text:
A garden bed is built so that it falls $1$ cm for every $25$ cm measured horizontally.
Find the angle the surface of the bed makes with the horizontal, correct to the nearest minute.
mastery.solution_text:
The fall is opposite the angle and the horizontal measurement is adjacent to it.
$\tan\theta=\frac{1}{25}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{25}\right)$
$=2.2906\ldots^{\circ}$
$=2^{\circ}17'26.20''$
$\approx2^{\circ}17'$
